hints.title: Greedy Outer Chunks
hints.text: Finding matching prefix and suffix substrings as early as possible never hurts future decomposition opportunities.

hints.title: Iterative Frontier Slicing
hints.text: Expand candidate prefix and suffix from opposite ends of the active string slice until a match is found.

hints.title: Chop and Add Count
hints.text: When prefix matches suffix, add 2 to chunk count and recurse or continue on the inner substring. If bounds meet with leftover characters, add 1.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def longestDecomposition(self, text: str) -> int:
        left, right = 0, len(text) - 1
        l_str = ""
        r_str = ""
        count = 0
        while left < right:
            l_str += text[left]
            r_str = text[right] + r_str
            if l_str == r_str:
                count += 2
                l_str = ""
                r_str = ""
            left += 1
            right -= 1
        if left == right or len(l_str) > 0:
            count += 1
        return count
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Full dynamic programming explores all chunk partitions, whereas the greedy matching property guarantees optimality.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Greedy string slice comparison operates with minimal auxiliary memory in linear or quadratic string comparison time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that matching the shortest prefix and suffix greedily maximizes total chunks.
complexity.notes: Can be accelerated to O(N) using rolling hashes.
